subject: Clarify billing for partially-finished streaming sessions and reconnects
messages:
From: Joe Brooks <joe.brooks@nimbushealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbushealth.com
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Question on streaming sessions billing (disconnect case)

Hi Rafael,

Quick question from our engineering and procurement teams while we evaluate Redwood for an internal POC. We kicked off a long streaming generation (approx 4k tokens target) and one of our client devices dropped the TCP connection mid-stream around ~80% output. When the client reconnected and retried, it resumed from the last acknowledged token and finished the generation.

Two answers would be helpful:
- What does Redwood bill in that scenario? Do you charge for the partial session + resumed tokens, or only for successfully emitted tokens?
- Is there any built-in grace window for reconnects/retries where you won't charge twice for overlapping in-flight tokens?

We saw a mention of "grace period" in the ratecard notes but not the exact rules; could you point us to the specific policy? Also attaching a short session log we captured.

Thanks,
Joe
Joe Brooks
Platform Engineer, Nimbus Health

Attachment: nimbus_poc_session_log_snippet.txt (text)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Joe Brooks <joe.brooks@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbushealth.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 10:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Question on streaming sessions billing (disconnect case)

Hi Joe — thanks for the clear example, and for sharing the log. Short answer up front: we bill on tokens emitted by the model and we apply a short reconnect window to avoid double-billing most client-side transient reconnects. Longer explanation below.

Policy summary (hosted API streaming):
- Billing unit: tokens actually emitted by the model and delivered to Redwood's streaming pipeline. If a token is never emitted (generation aborted server-side before token emission), it is not charged.
- In-flight grace window: by default we maintain a 20-second reconnect window tied to the session_id. If the client reconnects with the same session_id within that window and resumes, we attempt to attribute resumed output to the original session so you are not billed twice for overlapping token ranges.
- Server-side preemption / repeated retries: if the model restarts server-side (different model run id) or the session_id changes, we treat it as a new session and billing will reflect both runs unless a manual credit is issued.
- Partial generations: if your device disconnected and then resumed within the 20s window and we continued the same run, you'll only be billed for the union of emitted tokens — effectively the final output tokens. If the client re-sends prompts that cause re-generation of tokens already emitted, that could be billed twice.

Example against your 4k-token case:
- If the client disconnected at 3.2k emitted tokens and reconnected after 10s with the same session_id and we resumed the run, you will be billed for ~4k tokens total (not 3.2k + 4k).
- If the client reconnected after 5 minutes (outside the 20s window) and started a fresh run, you'd see billing for 3.2k + 4k unless we apply a credit.

We also provide an optional "session resume token" header that clients can pass to make attribution stricter for flaky networks; our SDKs set this by default.

Attaching the current streaming ratecard and a short note on the session window: redwood_streaming_ratecard_v2.pdf. If you want, I can get finance to run a quick example invoice for your POC runs so you can see how it appears on an invoice.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0198

Attachment: redwood_streaming_ratecard_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: Joe Brooks <joe.brooks@nimbushealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbushealth.com
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Question on streaming sessions billing (disconnect case)

Thanks Rafael — that helps. A couple clarifying questions so our procurement can sign off:

1) How do credits show up on the invoice if we request an adjustment for a POC? Is it line-item reversal, or a separate credit note?
2) For our mobile clients we see occasional 10–30s blips. If reconnects happen within the 20s window but the client resends the final prompt chunk (causing some overlap), will your attribution logic dedupe those tokens automatically or do we need to upload a session transcript for review?

Also curious whether you offer a limited POC credit for early POC customers if we commit to a 12-month hosted contract. We'd aim for a capped test budget but want to avoid surprise billing during the mobile tests.

—Joe

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Joe Brooks <joe.brooks@nimbushealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 09:17:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Question on streaming sessions billing (disconnect case)

Joe — good follow-ups. Answers below and looping in Marissa and Sean on the POC credit request.

1) Invoice presentation: POC adjustments are issued as separate credit memos tied to the invoice number. We can also issue a line-item reversal for a single invoice if you prefer — finance can do either, but credit memos are our default so your accounting team can match it easily.

2) Overlap dedupe behavior: our pipeline tries to dedupe obvious byte-range/token overlaps if the same session_id and resume token are present. We don't automatically dedupe across semantically-changed retries (e.g., if your client sends a tweaked prompt that causes re-generation, that is billable). If you want us to be aggressive about dedupe during the POC, we can enable an "attribution review" flag for the POC runs and have CS/Finance apply automated overlap credits within defined thresholds.

3) POC credit / commercial: Marissa — can you confirm what we can offer for a mid-size POC from a new mid-market customer? Joe, if you share an expected token cap for the POC (example: 200k tokens over 2 weeks), we can draft a credit proposal and show how credits would appear on test invoices.

[INTERNAL] Recommended commercial: Offer a one-time 30% credit on streaming usage for the first POC invoice (cap to $5k credit) and enable attribution review for POC session_ids. This keeps risk limited but protects Nimbus from transient duplicate charges. Marissa / Sean — ok to proceed?

Best,
Rafael

Thanks Rafael — reviewed and happy to approve the recommended commercial.

Proposal we can commit to:
- One-time 30% credit applied to the first POC invoice (cap $5,000).
- Enable attribution review for flagged session_ids during the POC window — CS will run automated overlap detection and request credits up to the cap.
- If Nimbus signs a 12-month hosted commitment within 30 days of POC completion, we'll roll the agreed POC credit into a one-time bill credit and provide a 5% committed-volume discount for the first three months.

Joe — if that looks acceptable I'll open a quick approval request to finance and send you the proposed credit memo language (and a short DocuSign for the POC terms amendment).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
